description: The National Household Travel Survey is the United States' national inventory of daily travel, run by the Federal Highway Administration. Each survey records every trip made by sampled households and their members over a 24-hour period, with trip purpose, mode (car, walking, bus, subway and others), travel time, time of day and day of week, alongside household, person and vehicle characteristics, for urban and rural areas. The series began in 1969 and recurs every five to seven years (Nationwide Personal Transportation Surveys of 1969, 1983, 1990 and 1995, then the NHTS); the 2022 NHTS covers January 2022 to January 2023 with 7,893 households. The NextGen NHTS moves to a biennial survey (7,500 households in the field from November 2024 to November 2025) and adds annual national passive origin-destination data for passengers and trucks for 2020 to 2024 produced by the University of Maryland. Public-use files, documentation, weighted occupancy factors and an online analysis tool are available free from the Oak Ridge National Laboratory site; the 1969 file is also archived on Harvard Dataverse. Caveats: samples are small for sub-state analysis, methods and questions change between editions, and the website depends on JavaScript. The survey supports travel demand and agent-based models, resilience planning of dependence on transport infrastructure, and safety and energy studies; it is related to the NTAD record and the Freight Analysis Framework.
